---
description: Audit a repo's agent config (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md) against registered concerns with `fathom config audit`, and apply fixes as the session — fathom reports, you edit.
argument-hint: [REPO=<path>]
---

<!-- fathom:owned — generated by `fathom init --skills`; safe to delete this line to adopt the file as your own -->

> **Capability note.** This file is rendered for Codex CLI's custom-prompts
> convention (`~/.codex/prompts/fathom-custodian.md`, invoked as
> `/prompts:fathom-custodian`). If your Codex CLI version has adopted the
> native `SKILL.md`-based skills mechanism (`.agents/skills/`), prefer
> copying this skill's `SKILL.md` there instead — the full version lives
> beside this file.

Run `fathom config audit` in the target repo. Read each finding honestly:
`holds` / `violated (file:line evidence)` / `unable-to-check (reason)` /
`off (named)`. For violations, YOU make the edit — update the instruction
to match reality, or create what the config promises — then re-run the
audit and report holds. Register new concerns in `.fathom/concerns.cue`
(repo governs) or `~/.fathom/concerns.cue` (user defaults): falsifiable
wants only — `forbidden_pattern`, `command_documented_and_exists`,
`max_lines`, `pointers_resolve` — each with a `why` naming a failure that
actually happened. Codex has no session hooks, so the attention line never
fires here: run the audit yourself at session start, the same way AGENTS.md
tells you to run `fathom thread brief`.
